title: studio-verdict.v1
description: The record of one creative-studio judgement. The RUNNER writes `runner` and the identity fields (scripts/studio_verdict.py skeleton); the CRITIC fills `critic`. scripts/studio_verdict.py check reads this file for the shape and adds the rules a schema cannot say; each rule is named in the description of the field it guards. Keywords used here are limited to the ones the checker implements (tests/test_studio_verdict.py holds that).

work_kind.description: rendered: floor rows carry viewport and element. text: floor rows carry a text locator.

mode.description: full: two reads, the second with the order swapped. light: one read.

borrow_max.description: From the profile. `critic.borrowed` may not hold more entries (borrow_over_max).

text_locator.description: A place in a text variant: the heading it sits under (empty for the whole document) and the paragraph number under that heading (0 for the whole section).

floor_row.description: One neutral-floor measurement of one variant. Rendered work: viewport and element are required. Text work: locator is required (floor_row_scope). A variant is ELIGIBLE when every blocking row of its latest capture has result pass; not_run is not a pass.

runner.description: Written by the runner. `check` refuses a record whose runner part or identity fields differ from the skeleton it is given (runner_part_altered).

variants.description: Unlabelled ids variant-1..variant-N, each once and in sequence (variant_ids). Nothing here says which seat or house made a variant.

read_orders.description: The randomised order of each read. Each is a permutation of the variant ids; full mode holds two, the second the first reversed; light mode holds one (read_order).

recaptures.description: Later captures of a repaired variant, in sequence 1, 2, ... (for text work: the claim check re-run). A re-capture must carry every blocking row of the variant's first capture, by row id and, for rendered work, width (repair_recapture_incomplete); a variant whose latest re-capture is incomplete is not eligible.

borrow.description: A named part of a LOSING variant that the winner re-makes. Every card says what the part is and why it is worth having. fragment: a locator of the kind of work, markup (a selector) for rendered work and text (a heading and a paragraph) for written work, and nothing else (borrow_locator). system: anchor; rendered work anchors in direction_contract or root_style, text work in direction_contract, outline or term_set (borrow_anchor). move: technique and an evidence_region of the kind of work: for rendered work evidence (a reference the runner recorded for that variant), with or without area, and never text; for written work text and nothing else (borrow_move). `from` is a losing variant (borrow_source).

why.description: The line of the brief or the rubric criterion this part serves. The winner re-makes the part from this card.

critic.description: Filled by the critic. The skeleton leaves could_not_judge and open_to_user null: the critic must replace each with a list, which may be empty.

reads.description: One entry per read order, numbered from 1 (reads_mismatch). pick is the variant that read chose, or null when it found no winner. When two reads pick differently, open_to_user must hold an order_flip entry (flip_not_open_to_user).

tells.description: Per variant, what was judged against that variant's OWN direction contract. One entry per variant (tells_missing). A tell names an axis of that contract; it never compares variants. A run may give the critic blocking floor rows of its own to fill. Each is exactly one entry per variant whose axis is the row id, with held true as a pass: `first-screen` (first_screen_row_missing, winner_fails_first_screen) and, in a run with a truth pack, `unlisted-statements`, false when the draft states a fact that is on no claim list and not in the truth pack (unlisted_statements_row_missing, winner_states_an_unlisted_fact). The winner's entry must hold.

rubric.description: The comparison by visitor mode and brief: the only ground on which variants are compared. Not empty when the outcome is winner (rubric_empty). At least one row favours the winner (winner_not_favoured), and `favours` names a variant of this record or `none` (rubric_favours_unknown).

outcome.description: winner needs an eligible winner (winner_ineligible) or a confirmed repair. no_award is required when no variant is eligible (no_award_required).

winner.description: A variant id when the outcome is winner (winner_missing, winner_unknown); null when it is no_award (winner_with_no_award). It is one of the reads' picks (winner_not_picked). Its LATEST capture passes every blocking row, or it is a confirmed repair (winner_ineligible): a variant that passed first and fails after a re-capture cannot win as it stands. A winner that has any re-capture was changed after the verdict opened: it is accepted only with `repair` naming its LATEST re-capture, rejudged and confirmed both true, whatever its first capture said (winner_not_rejudged).

selected_for_repair.description: true: the winner failed a blocking row and was picked to be repaired. Accepted only with `repair` pointing at the winner's LATEST re-capture, that re-capture passing every blocking row, and rejudged and confirmed both true (repair_no_recapture, repair_recapture_fails, repair_recapture_incomplete, repair_not_rejudged).

no_award.description: Required with outcome no_award, null otherwise. all_fail_blocking only when no variant is eligible; otherwise brief_line_unmet with the line of the brief no variant met (no_award_unexplained).

rejected.description: Losing variants nothing is taken from, each with the reason. Every losing variant is in borrowed or here; with no_award every variant is here (loser_unaccounted). The winner is never here (rejected_unknown).

could_not_judge.description: What the critic could not judge from the evidence. Required; may be an empty list.

open_to_user.description: Questions only the user can settle. Required; may be an empty list.
